newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Gabon's Bongo proposes July 14 Brazzaville truce.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's Bongo proposes July 14 Brazzaville truce.

text.p: Gabon's veteran president, Omar Bongo, is trying to rally the warring parties in the battered Congo Republic capital Brazzaville around a July 14 ceasefire, a spokesman for one of them said on Thursday.

Francois Iboovi, spokesman for former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, told Reuters by telephone that Sassou was studying the proposals for a truce between his militia and President Pascal Lissouba's forces, and would reply shortly.

The proposals, part of a mediation bid to steer the Central African oil-producing nation towards peace negotiations, were taken to Brazzaville by U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, who later returned to Gabon's capital Libreville.
"We have received the proposals from Omar Bongo and we are studying them. The date for the ceasefire is part of the proposals. It won't be long before we respond," Iboovi said.
Earlier, a U.N. source said Sahnoun had had talks with Sassou and Lissouba during his brief shuttle to the city. Lissouba's response was not immediately clear.
The showdown, which began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias, has killed hundreds of people, mainly civilians.

Iboovi said the Bongo proposals dealt almost exclusively with conditions for a ceasefire. A July 1 attempt by Bongo to broker a ceasefire failed, with Sassou demanding that Lissouba sign instead of his prime minister.
Aid workers said Brazzaville was relatively calm on Thursday despite some sporadic shooting.

Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas is heading a national mediation effort. His militia were at the heart of similar political and ethnic clashes which killed at least 2,000 people after a disputed 1993 election.
Lissouba had been planning to run for re-election on July 27. Sassou and Kolelas were also planning to stand.
